title: What is known about 1RB1RF_1RC0RA_1LD1RB_1LE0LD_0RA0LB_0RB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RF_1RC0RA_1LD1RB_1LE0LD_0RA0LB_0RB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean (kernel) proves the halting configurations, no halt in the first 10,000 steps (107 with native_decide) and three shift rules. Direct C runs find no halt in 2·1010 steps and show the word-and-counter structure described below; the map of the left-end rebuilds, which is where a halt could happen, is not known.

Round 6, the proved neighbours. busycoq (pull request 36) proves the machines that differ from this one only in the entry E0. That entry is used from the first steps of this run and again and again (24 times in the first 1010 steps (10 in the first 103, 18 in 104, 20 in 105, 22 in 106, 23 in 107, 24 in 109)), and each use leaves a different left end than in the neighbours, so their proof does not carry over. No transfer; the question stays open.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: W 0 1^3 0 1^(2k+1) B>0 0 → W 0 1 0 1 0 1 1 C> 0^(2k) 1 (head on the first of the 2k 0s) in 2k+11 steps (the last block erased after a record); B> (10)^k → (01)^k B> and B> (01)^k → (11)^k B> in 2k steps.

claims.title: What the entry E0 does, and the two halting patterns
claims.text: The entry fires when D, erasing 1s leftwards, reads a 0 with another 0 on its left: four steps later (D0, E0, A1, F0) the cells read 0 1 0 and B is on the next cell to the right. The machine halts from exactly two local patterns, each proved in Lean to halt whatever else is on the tape: C reading a 0 with two 0s on its left (0 0 C>0) and B reading 1 1 1. That there is no other way to halt is read backwards from the table (an argument on paper, not in Lean).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 249 cells have been visited and 135 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: Direct C runs (tools/c/tmrun.c, and c/fevents.c of 1RB0RF_1LC1RE_0LD0LC_1RD0RB_1RA0RB_0LC---) reach 2·1010 steps; there are 238 F events (A reading 1), each followed by a 0.

claims.title: The entry E0 is used from the start and keeps being used
claims.text: In the run from blank tape the entry E0 is first used at step 6; 24 times in the first 1010 steps (10 in the first 103, 18 in 104, 20 in 105, 22 in 106, 23 in 107, 24 in 109). The proved neighbours use their version of the entry too (the neighbour with 1LB in the first machine's lettering: 11 times in 1010 steps), so the difference is not an unused entry: it changes the run.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/fixed
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.016).

claims.title: Records are words; time doubles
claims.text: At every record of the first 2·1010 steps outside the left-end rebuilds the tape is a word ending in 1^n B>0, n grows by 2 per record (to 57), the rest changes by one local rewrite, and the time between records tends to double.

claims.title: Halting only at the left end
claims.text: A reads a 1 (the only way to F) only while the left end of the word is rebuilt, after the moving rewrite has reached it (some of these rebuilds are restarts of the last block).
claims.where: F events of the direct run

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The record-to-record map and the map of the left-end rebuilds have not been derived, so there is no accelerated simulation beyond direct runs.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine writes a word of blocks of 1s whose last block grows by 2 at every record while the time between records doubles; it could only stop during rare rebuilds of the left end of the word, and none of the few seen so far did.

facts.text: No halt in a direct run; 238 F events.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
Last block of the word at the last record seen.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.016).
After 109 steps the tape spans 249 cells (20 left of the start, 228 right), with a density of 1s of 0.542.

The tape (run-length coded, 1^5 is five 1s, C>0 the head in state C on a 0) at some of the last moments the head reached a new cell, cut to 400 characters:

sections.heading: At every record, a word
html: This machine and 1RB0RF_1RC0RA_1LD1RB_1LE0LD_1LB0LB_0RB--- differ only in A1 and E0, and they behave the same way. Each time the head reaches a new cell on the right (a record), the tape is a word: blocks of 1s separated by single 0s, ending in 1^n B>0. For this machine, a short gadget with double 0s (1 0 0 1 0 0 1 0 1 0 1 1 0 1 0 1 0 0 at the last record) sits at the left end, then the word. The blocks are odd, except that the first may be 2.

From one record to the next the last block grows by 2. The rest of the word changes by one small, width-preserving rewrite, at a place that moves one block to the left per record. The rewrites seen are 3 1 1 → 1 1 3, b → (b−2) 1, 5 1 1 → 3 1 3, 3 3 3 1 1 1 → 1 1 3 5 3 and a few others. The time between records tends to double. In the first 2·1010 steps the last block reaches 57 (record at step 1.99·1010).

sections.heading: Two counters
html: Right after a record, state D erases the last block from right to left. Only a single marker 1 remains, n+1 cells out. This is the Lean theorem rec_erase: W 0 1^3 0 1^(2k+1) B>0 0 becomes W 0 1 0 1 0 1 1 C> 0^(2k) 1 (the head on the first of the 2k 0s) in 2k+11 steps. The head then zigzags. Going left, it turns the single-1 blocks at the end of the word into units 1 1 0 0. Going right, B sweeps them back, turning 10 into 01 and 01 into 11 (b_sweep10, b_sweep01). Meanwhile the empty stretch fills with gaps 1 0^odd.

Between two records of 1RB0RF_1RC0RA_1LD1RB_1LE0LD_1LB0LB_0RB---, the turning points follow a ruler sequence on both sides of a fixed cell. On the right they go 88, 90, 88, 92, 88, 90, 88, 94, …. On the left they dig 55, 65, 41, 65, 55, 65, 45, … cells deep into the word. This is the signature of two binary counters running against each other: one written in the end of the word, one in the gaps. A full count takes about 2n/2 steps, and it ends at the next record.

sections.heading: Rebuilds and F events
html: F is reached only from A reading a 1, and F halts on a 1. So a halt needs A to read 1 1. In the runs, A reads a 1 only when the moving rewrite reaches the left end of the word. There the machine rebuilds the left end. Some of these rebuilds also extend the word, and the last block starts again small (a restart). Records during a rebuild need not be words, and the F events come in bursts there. In the first 2·1010 steps there are 238 F events, and each is followed by a 0.

Rebuilds are rare. For 1RB0RF_1RC0RA_1LD1RB_1LE0LD_1LB0LB_0RB--- the restarts come at about 5·103, 1.4·104, 3.1·105, 1.5·107, 9.7·107 and 7.0·109 steps. They are rare because the rewrite moves one block per record and records come ever more slowly, so direct simulation sees only a handful. Deciding the machine needs the exact record-to-record map on words, and from it the map of the left-end rebuilds. Neither is written down yet.
Status: open. Lean has the halting configurations, no halt in 107 steps, and three shift rules of the sweeps. The record structure is observed in direct runs, not proved.

sections.heading: The proved neighbours
html: The community tracker notes: one table, three starts, one entry away from a machine proved in busycoq's pull request 36. This machine is one start of the table; 1RB0RE_1LC1RA_1LD0LC_0RE0LA_1RA1RF_0RA--- is the same table started in this machine's state B, and 1RB0RA_0LC0RE_1LE1LD_0LE---_1LF0LC_1RA1LE is the mirrored table started in state D. The proved machines are 1RB1RF_1RC0RA_1LD1RB_1LE0LD_1LA0LB_0RB---, 1RB1RF_1RC0RA_1LD1RB_1LE0LD_1LB0LB_0RB--- and 1RB1RF_1RC0RA_1LD1RB_1LE0LD_1RB0LB_0RB--- (E0 = 1LA, 1LB, 1RB; here 0RA): the same table except for the entry E0.

The entry fires when D, erasing 1s leftwards, reads a 0 with another 0 on its left: four steps later (D0, E0, A1, F0) the cells read 0 1 0 and B is on the next cell to the right. In the neighbours the same moment writes a 1 there instead and carries on differently (to the left for 1L, to the right for 1R).

The entry is used 24 times in the first 1010 steps (10 in the first 103, 18 in 104, 20 in 105, 22 in 106, 23 in 107, 24 in 109). So the proof cannot be carried over by showing the entry is never reached. The neighbours' proofs are long inductions over a word-and-counter description of each machine's own run (about 1,200 to 1,700 lines of Coq each); they depend on what this entry leaves at the left end of the word, and we did not find a replacement invariant for this machine. The tracker says the same in its own words: the rare entry keeps changing the head of the word.
What Lean adds here is small: the effect of the entry, and the two local patterns from which the machine halts (C reading a 0 with two 0s on its left (0 0 C>0); B reading 1 1 1).

summary: At every record a word of blocks with a last block growing by 2 and doubling time; halting only possible at rare rebuilds of the left end; open. One entry (E0) away from machines proved in busycoq; the entry is used again and again, so that proof does not transfer.
